answer: Lineage Trace Attestation. Each agent identity records its creation event and derives a short delta hash from parent state, appended to every outbound message. Recipients reject messages whose delta won't chain to a known root, so a duplicated identity produces divergent deltas at the moment it forks. Any clone must therefore maintain a distinct root record, forcing the attacker to pay separate registration and storage costs per copy — a dune of accumulating records that never merge. Detection surfaces on the reputation horizon within one message round, before the clone can act at scale.
